title: Supplier-Driven Strategies and Customer Outcomes in Dropshipping: The Roles of Trust and Platform Transparency
affiliations: Cyprus International University, Near East University and Near East University

detail.title: Supplier-Driven Strategies and Customer Outcomes in Dropshipping: The Roles of Trust and Platform Transparency
detail.abstract: This study investigates how supplier-driven strategies influence key customer outcomes within the dropshipping business model. Specifically, it investigates the effects of supplier reliability, supplier-related efficiencies, and supplier management practices on repeat purchasing behavior, customer satisfaction, and customer complaints. It also tests whether customer trust mediates the link between supplier reliability and repeat purchasing and whether platform transparency moderates the relationship between supplier management and customer complaints.Adopting a quantitative, positivist approach, data were collected through a structured online survey from 300 participants across Iran, Turkey, Cyprus, the United States, Germany, and several African countries. Judgmental sampling ensured participants had prior experience with e-commerce or dropshipping transactions. Measurement reliability and validity were evaluated through Cronbach’s alpha, composite reliability, and convergent validity tests. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was used to assess direct, mediating, and moderating hypothesesThe findings indicate that supplier reliability significantly enhances repeat purchasing, and supplier-related efficiencies strongly improve customer satisfaction. Supplier management practices also significantly reduce customer complaints. However, customer trust did not mediate the supplier reliability–repeat purchasing relationship, and platform transparency did not moderate the influence of supplier management on complaints. These results suggest that performance-based factors play a stronger role than relational or transparency cues in dropshipping contexts. By integrating operational, relational, and platform-related variables within a cross-cultural SEM framework, this research offers novel empirical evidence on how supplier performance shapes customer customer behavior in global digital marketplaces.

detail.title: The Role of Social Power: Online Promotion, Consumer Engagement and Sales
detail.abstract: Recognizing the critical role of online promotions in shaping consumer decisions, this study examines how online promotions affect consumer engagement and sales across purchase funnel stages, focusing on the moderating roles of social power—specifically, sellers’ persuasive power and buyers’ bargaining power. Proposing a novel measure of social power, an empirical model based on unique data from a leading e-commerce platform shows that strong seller persuasive power significantly amplifies the positive effect of promotions on engagement, whereas high buyer bargaining power strengthens the impact of engagement on sales. Notably, both moderating effects are more pronounced on mobile platforms. These findings offer fresh insights into social power dynamics in e-commerce and provide actionable guidance for designing more effective online promotional strategies.

detail.title: How to make the optimal bundling strategy on multi-product bundling within a rebate bundling sale cycle
detail.abstract: This paper focuses on the optimal bundling problem in retail markets with rebate bundling sales, investigating the optimal bundle proportion and quantity for rebate bundling sales.  This study introduces mutual customer purchasing intentions and bundled-rebate factors in multi-product bundling, and establishes an optimal model for the expected bundling strategy and expected profit of rebate bundling sales based on the cumulated expected profits from bundled items. A convergent algorithm for numerical calculation of the optimal expected bundling strategy is proposed. Furthermore, an optimal bundling profit model under the functional relationship between bundled-rebate factor and bundled quantity is established, and a convergent algorithm for solving the optimal bundling strategy of this model is proposed. Finally, numerical analysis results show that the optimal expected bundling strategy and the maximum expected profit can be obtained. The impact of rebate value on multi-product bundling in rebate bundling sales is revealed.

title: Audience Behavior Parallels Systematic Differences in Fear-Based Language on Fox News and CNN

detail.title: Audience Behavior Parallels Systematic Differences in Fear-Based Language on Fox News and CNN

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors do not have any personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced their study.

detail.abstract: CNN and Fox News each reach millions of people daily, but Fox News exerts much stronger influence on public opinion and behavior. We test one plausible explanation for this: systematic differences in fear, which is a potent driver of attitudes and actions. We create a publicly available database of 997,902 headlines from cnn.com and foxnews.com spanning 2020-21, then analyze fear-based language across topics. We show that Fox News uses more fear than CNN, on average. However, Fox News used less fear than CNN in its COVID-19 pandemic coverage, and more fear in its vaccine side effect and mandate coverage. These findings offer a plausible explanation for Fox News viewers’ lower compliance with public health measures and lower vaccination rates, and may help explain how Fox News generally exerts such strong influence.

title: How Can School Principals in Indonesia Use Appreciative Inquiry (AI) to Promote Technology Integration
affiliations: University of Adelaide

detail.title: How Can School Principals in Indonesia Use Appreciative Inquiry (AI) to Promote Technology Integration
detail.abstract: Technology integration has become a critical priority for advancing Indonesia’s educational quality and supporting the nation’s long-term vision of Indonesia Emas 2045. However, Indonesian schools continue to face persistent challenges, including financial constraints, uneven digital literacy, and cultural resistance toward adopting educational technologies. This essay examines how school principals can leverage Appreciative Inquiry (AI) as a strengths-based leadership approach to promote effective and sustainable technology integration. Unlike problem-focused models of change, AI emphasises identifying existing assets, amplifying successful practices, and fostering collective ownership of innovation. Through the lens of the 4D-Cycle—Discovery, Dream, Design, and Destiny, this essay illustrates how Indonesian school leaders can mobilise teachers, students, parents, and community stakeholders to build shared visions of future-ready learners, co-design contextually relevant technology plans, and reinforce long-term digital transformation. Drawing on international research and Indonesian policy contexts, the essay highlights how AI principles can help principals reinterpret centralised directives, cultivate collaborative cultures, and initiate incremental yet meaningful digital practices, such as optimising existing digital tools and aligning school budgets with technological priorities. The discussion also frames the COVID-19 pandemic as a catalyst for educational reform, demonstrating that schools with stronger digital readiness and adaptive leadership were better positioned to navigate remote learning. Ultimately, this essay argues that Appreciative Inquiry offers Indonesian principals a practical, positive, and participatory pathway to embed technology integration as an enduring organisational practice rather than a temporary response to crisis.

detail.title: Hafiz Saeed’s Shadow Over Bangladesh- Pakistan’s New Eastern Jihad
detail.abstract: This book examines the emerging security threat posed by Pakistan-linked extremist networks operating across Bangladesh, situating Hafiz Saeed’s ideological and organisational influence as a central vector in the resurgence of transnational jihadist activity along India’s vulnerable eastern frontier. While Pakistan’s use of non-state actors as instruments of statecraft has historically focused on the western theatre—Kashmir and Afghanistan—new evidence indicates a strategic eastward shift, with Bangladesh increasingly exploited as a permissive operational space. This study analyses the ideological diffusion, recruitment pipelines, covert financial channels, and logistical networks that connect Lashkar-e-Taiba–aligned actors to radical elements embedded within Bangladesh’s socio-political landscape. Using a synthesis of open-source intelligence, field-level reporting, security assessments, and historical patterns of Pakistan’s proxy warfare, the book investigates how these linkages are shaping a new “Eastern Jihad Doctrine,” designed to encircle India through multi-directional sub-conventional pressure. It also explores institutional vulnerabilities within Bangladesh, including political polarisation, refugee-driven destabilisation, and porous border ecologies, which collectively enable external manipulation. The analysis situates these developments within the larger Indo-Pacific strategic environment, offering a comprehensive assessment of how Pakistan’s intelligence apparatus may be repurposing jihadist ecosystems to undermine India’s security from the east. The study concludes by outlining policy implications for India, Bangladesh, and regional partners, emphasising the need for intelligence fusion, counter-radicalisation frameworks, and a coordinated deterrence posture to pre-empt the consolidation of a new Pakistani-backed jihadist front in the Bay of Bengal littoral.

title: Welfare and Fiscal Effects of Adopting a Notional Defined Contribution Pension System
affiliations: University of Bologna Department of Statistics, Prometeia and Ca’ Foscari University of Venice - Department of Economics

detail.title: Welfare and Fiscal Effects of Adopting a Notional Defined Contribution Pension System
detail.abstract: This paper quantifies the macroeconomic and inter-generational welfare effects of Italy's 1995 Dini reform, which replaced the Defined Benefit (DB) Pay-As-You-Go (PAYG) pension system with a Notional Defined Contribution (NDC) scheme. Using a large-scale Overlapping Generations (OLG) model calibrated to Italian data, we simulate the transition from a DB to an NDC regime under United Nations demographic projections. The model embeds endogenous human capital accumulation and replicates the institutional details of Italy's NDC accounting rules. Results show that the reform improves long-run fiscal sustainability and aggregate welfare, though transitional cohorts face temporary welfare losses. The NDC framework increases labor supply and savings, mitigating the adverse macroeconomic effects of population aging. The paper provides a fully calibrated assessment of a transition from Defined Benefit to Notional Defined Contribution pensions, within a general equilibrium framework, linking demographic change, human capital, and fiscal sustainability.

detail.abstract:
This article critically examines the emerging strategic realignments in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR), focusing on the intensifying trilateral interplay between the United States, Pakistan, and Maldives, alongside the parallel rise of US–Sri Lanka military cooperation. Drawing on publicly available defence agreements, naval deployments, UAV acquisitions, and high-level military exchanges, the analysis argues that India’s maritime bastion—long considered secure relative to its historically vulnerable northern land front—is undergoing unprecedented encirclement pressures. The study foregrounds Pakistan’s rapidly expanding defence footprint in the Maldives through successive high-level visits, Passage Exercises (PASSEX), and a growing influence over Maldivian maritime security infrastructure, including Turkish-supplied Bayraktar UCAVs with precision-strike capabilities. Simultaneously, the strategic US–Sri Lanka Defence MOU of 2025, integrating Sri Lanka’s armed forces with the Montana National Guard and US Coast Guard District 13, signals a potential increase in US maritime presence near India’s southern littoral.

The article situates these developments within a broader geopolitical framework shaped by China’s historical arming of Sri Lanka, Pakistan’s efforts to regain naval access in the Bay of Bengal (for the first time since 1971), and Washington’s deepening interest in the Bay of Bengal’s gas reserves and maritime trade routes. It further analyses the emerging interoperability among Maldives-Pakistan-Turkey military technologies, the US Navy’s blue-water logistics capabilities, and Sri Lanka’s expanding inventory of Chinese, Pakistani, and American systems—highlighting their combined implications for India’s naval freedom of manoeuvre, anti-submarine warfare posture, and supply chain security in the peninsula.

title: Merit versus Race and Gender: A Constitutional & Ethical Critique of Identity-Based Hiring in Higher Education
affiliations: Metropolitan State University of Denver

detail.title: Merit versus Race and Gender: A Constitutional & Ethical Critique of Identity-Based Hiring in Higher Education

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced their study.

detail.abstract: This paper critically evaluates Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) hiring mandates in higher education and assesses their compatibility with constitutional and merit-based principles. Integrating constitutional law, empirical research, and ethical analysis, the study argues that DEI-driven frameworks redefine fairness from equality of opportunity to equality of outcomes, thereby conflicting with the Fourteenth Amendment, Title VII, and the Supreme Court's 2023 Students for Fair Admissions decision. Empirical evidence, including metaanalyses on corporate diversity, DEI training, and hiring outcomes, reveals weak or negative effects, widespread reverse discrimination, and the proliferation of symbolic compliance mechanisms. The paper contends that demographic engineering undermines academic freedom, intellectual diversity, and institutional integrity. As an alternative, it advances Constructive Ethnic Studies, shared moral foundations, and viewpoint diversity as constitutionally sound pathways that promote genuine inclusion. The analysis concludes that raceneutral, merit-based hiring best upholds legal equality, academic excellence, and the core purposes of higher education.

title: Measuring Corruption from Text Data
affiliations: Central European University

detail.title: Measuring Corruption from Text Data
detail.abstract: Using Brazilian municipal audit reports, I construct an automated corruption index that combines a dictionary of audit irregularities with principal component analysis. The index validates strongly against independent human coders, explaining 71-73 % of the variation in hand-coded corruption counts in samples where coders themselves exhibit high agreement, and the results are robust within these validation samples. The index behaves as theory predicts, correlating with municipal characteristics that prior research links to corruption. Supervised learning alternatives yield nearly identical municipal rankings (R 2 = 0.98), confirming that the dictionary approach captures the same underlying construct. The method scales to the full audit corpus and offers advantages over both manual coding and Large Language Models (LLMs) in transparency, cost, and long-run replicability.

title: Short-and Long-Term Mechanisms Behind the Child Penalty: Evidence from South Korea
affiliations: Seoul National University

detail.title: Short-and Long-Term Mechanisms Behind the Child Penalty: Evidence from South Korea
detail.abstract: Using a 26-year longitudinal panel dataset from Korea, covering five years before and twenty years after childbirth, this study tracks the evolution of the evolution of the long-term gender wage gap and analyzes the short-and long-term mechanisms underlying its dynamics following childbirth. The gap widens asymmetrically, driven by women's labor market exit in the short run and declining hourly wages in the long run. Labor market exit stems from rigid working-hour structures, while wage declines result from transitions into unstable employment. Moreover, women who leave the labor market earlier after childbirth are more exposed to unstable employment.

title: Does the Top Manager’s Profile Influence Sustainable Development in Local Governments? Evidence from Brazil

detail.title: Does the Top Manager’s Profile Influence Sustainable Development in Local Governments? Evidence from Brazil
detail.abstract: This study analyzes the influence of the top manager's profile on sustainable development in local governments. In this research, we investigate 184 municipalities of the State of Ceará, northeastern Brazil, from 2009 to 2016. Data was analyzed through descriptive statistics and econometric models estimated by FGLS method for panel data. The results show that sustainable development is influenced by the following top manager's attributes: age, socioeconomic status, experience, education, and political orientation. From a theoretical perspective, the study provides evidence that the Upper Echelons Theory is consistent and applicable in the public sector, and expands the theory by including political orientation, which emerged as a relevant manager's attribute.

detail.title: Spatial Reconfiguration of Tourism: New Dynamics of Rural Development

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced their study.

detail.abstract: This study aims to analyse the new economic dynamics of tourism establishments in rural destinations by examining the factors influencing the centrifugal and centripetal forces that shape them, emphasising the impacts generated by the pandemic. For this purpose, the case of the tourist destination of Tapalpa, Jalisco, was studied using a mixed-methods approach. Initially, data was collected from official sources, academic studies on tourism and post-pandemic resilience, and through interviews with key local actors and structured observation. This data was then used to identify new patterns of tourist flow and dispersion about tourism establishments. The research finds that the disruption caused by COVID-19 acted as a centrifugal force, profoundly altering tourist preferences and consumption patterns, among other factors explored in the results.

title: Scaling Peer-to-Peer Food Sharing: The Hidden Costs of Adding Commercial Partners
affiliations: University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business,  and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Gies College of Business

detail.title: Scaling Peer-to-Peer Food Sharing: The Hidden Costs of Adding Commercial Partners
detail.abstract: Household food waste is a global challenge: one billion meals are discarded daily even as hunger and food insecurity persist, contributing to greenhouse-gas emissions. Digital platforms that let households give away surplus food can reduce waste at scale but rely on household participation. As they grow, platforms add commercial partners (supermarkets/bakeries) to source food and generate revenue, raising the question of how commercial channel entry affects household participation. We show this entry introduces a trade-off: while these partnerships expand reach and financial sustainability, they also create competition and discourage household sharing. Using proprietary data from a peer-to-peer food-sharing platform that introduced a commercial channel, which displays commercial posts alongside household posts in the same feed, we exploit the staggered rollout of the channel across 206 London wards. We find a short-lived 51% increase in successful posts-those that receive at least one pickup-across commercial and household posts, but this effect disappears. In contrast, successful household posts decline persistently-by 27% (47%) in the short (long) term-reducing redistribution from the hardest-to-reach waste segment and weakening the platform's mission. We trace the decline to (i) recipients' preference for commercial posts-household posts perform worse when nearby supply is denser and more commercial-and (ii) discouraged household contributions-households start posting less frequently. These findings highlight the trade-offs of scaling sociallyoriented platforms: commercial channel entry delivers short-term reach and revenue but can discourage household-to-household redistribution unless platforms adopt mechanisms that preserve visibility, trust, and motivation for household contributors as commercial activity expands.

AI.tldr: 商业渠道进入食品共享平台会带来权衡：虽然扩大了覆盖面和财务可持续性，但会与家庭分享形成竞争，导致家庭参与度下降。研究发现商业渠道引入后，家庭成功分享帖子短期下降27%，长期下降47%，削弱了平台减少家庭食物浪费的核心使命。
AI.research_question: 商业渠道进入如何影响家庭在食品共享平台上的参与度？
AI.motivation: 家庭食物浪费是全球性挑战，数字平台可减少浪费但依赖家庭参与。随着平台发展，引入商业合作伙伴以扩大覆盖和创收，但这对家庭参与的影响尚不清楚。
AI.theoretical_framework: 平台竞争理论、用户参与行为理论、社会导向平台的规模化权衡
AI.method: 利用伦敦206个区商业渠道分阶段推出的专有数据，采用准实验设计分析商业渠道进入对家庭参与的影响

AI.practical_contributions: 为平台设计者提供启示：在引入商业渠道时需要采取措施保护家庭贡献者的可见性、信任和动机，以维持平台的核心使命

title: Optimisation of Fire Evacuation Strategies for High-Rise Hospital Inpatient Department
affiliations: Changchun Institute of Technology, Changchun Institute of Technology, Changchun Institute of Technology, Changchun Institute of Technology, Changchun Institute of Technology, Northeast Normal University and Changchun Institute of Technology

detail.title: Optimisation of Fire Evacuation Strategies for High-Rise Hospital Inpatient Department
detail.abstract: Due to the vulnerability of patients and the diversity of the occupants, hospital inpatient units are more prone to congestion or even stagnation during evacuation, making fire evacuations in these settings more complex and hazardous compared to other types of buildings. Most existing studies have focused primarily on evacuation procedures, often neglecting the impact of fire scenarios on the evacuation process. In order to more thoroughly investigate the results of fire evacuation studies in high-rise hospital inpatient departments, this paper takes a specific hospital inpatient department as an example. PyroSim software is used to simulate fire scenarios, and through the analysis of temperature, visibility, and CO concentration, the available safe evacuation time is determined. Subsequently, based on the layout and distribution of occupants within the building, appropriate evacuation plans are designed. Pathfinder software is used to simulate different strategies, and the optimal evacuation strategy is ultimately determined. The results show that by reasonably adjusting the selection of exits and setting priorities for occupants, the evacuation efficiency can be significantly improved. The strategy of adjusting exit selection and setting refuge rooms reduces the required evacuation time by 559.9s compared to unorganized evacuation. The findings of this study provide a reasonable strategy for fire evacuation in high-rise hospital inpatient departments, which can effectively reduce casualties in such buildings and contribute to their safety management.

title: Multidimensional Poverty and Chars: A Study in Dhubri district of Assam
affiliations: Tezpur University and Tezpur University

detail.title: Multidimensional Poverty and Chars: A Study in Dhubri district of Assam
detail.abstract: The pathbreaking research work of Amartya Sen has given a new direction to poverty analysis which leads to a common agreement that poverty is a multidimensional phenomenon. The adoption of SDGs by UNDP develops a clear understanding of the concept of multidimensional poverty. In today's world, eradication of poverty is necessary for the development of human resources which ultimately paves the path of development in an economy. Assam, being one of the backward states of India suffers from the perennial problem of multidimensional poverty for many years. Char areas of Assam are socioeconomically backward and have the highest multidimensional poverty rate as compared to other regions of the state. The current study focuses on the issue of multidimensional poverty in the char areas of the Dhubri district of Assam by constructing a multidimensional poverty index. The article measures the multidimensional poverty index in five dimensions-education, health, standard of living, empowerment, and employment which are equally weighted. The findings reveal the gloomy picture of char areas as they are deprived in basic amenities of life. Moreover, the empowerment dimension is a significant contributor to multidimensional poverty which reflects the vulnerable conditions of the women in these areas. Therefore, a proper in-depth investigation of multidimensional poverty issue in char areas are necessary which shall help the policymakers in framing policies for the achievement of SDGs.

title: Partisan Universities and Political Donations
affiliations: Amazon and Universidad Adolfo Ibañez

detail.title: Partisan Universities and Political Donations
detail.abstract: This paper provides causal evidence that educational institutions shape political behavior and partisan engagement. Using population data linking Chilean college applications to political donations (2004-2021), we exploit score-based discontinuities in the centralized admission system to estimate the effect of attending universities with different ideological orientations. Enrollment at left-leaning universities raises the probability of donating to left-wing campaigns by 0.41 pp (equivalent to 40% of the baseline donation rate), with effects reaching 1.2 pp in public left-leaning universities and smaller but positive effects in private ones. High electoral exposure during college amplifies these left-leaning effects by an additional 35%, indicating that institutional influence is sensitive to political context. Attending a private right-leaning university reduces donations to the left by 0.44 pp, with no offsetting rise in rightwing donations. The results are stronger among earlier cohorts, indicating lasting effects of institutional exposure. Evidence by field of study shows no effect for left-leaning majors (social sciences excluding economics), whereas business/economics majors increase right-wing donations by 0.78 pp. The pattern is consistent with left-leaning engagement being associated with a public, collectivist institutional culture, while patterns on the right suggest mobilization through market-oriented curricula and associated professional networks.

AI.method: 利用智利集中录取系统中的分数断点设计，分析2004-2021年大学申请与政治捐款的关联数据

title: Deep Learning-Based Image Inspection Technology: Applications and an Innovative Segmentation Approach for Industrial Recognition
affiliations: Fujian Polytechnic Normal University, I-Shou University and I-Shou University

detail.title: Deep Learning-Based Image Inspection Technology: Applications and an Innovative Segmentation Approach for Industrial Recognition
detail.abstract: Deep learning-based image inspection has emerged as a powerful tool in both industrial manufacturing and medical diagnostics, offering high efficiency and reliability in anomaly detection. Among various computer vision tasks, image segmentation is particularly critical, as it partitions images into meaningful regions and enables accurate feature extraction from regions of interest. The quality of segmentation directly influences subsequent recognition processes and can determine overall system success. In industrial applications, such as defect detection in manufactured products, both accuracy and processing speed are key factors. Effective defect recognition relies heavily on precise object extraction, where deep learning segmentation techniques play a central role. This study investigates widely used segmentation approaches within deep learning frameworks and introduces a novel method optimized for industrial image inspection. The proposed technique improves model training efficiency, enhances segmentation accuracy, and accelerates processing speed. Experimental results demonstrate that the method meets the stringent accuracy demands of the industrial sector while ensuring real-time performance. These findings highlight the crucial role of segmentation in deep learning-based inspection and provide a practical solution with significant potential for deployment in real-world industrial applications.

title: The 2025 Nigerian Tax Reform Acts: Analysis of Key Provisions and Implementation Challenges
affiliations: University of Uyo (UNIUYO)

detail.title: The 2025 Nigerian Tax Reform Acts: Analysis of Key Provisions and Implementation Challenges
detail.abstract: In 2025, Nigeria rolled out a major tax reform, the biggest in decades. The country had been dealing with some serious issues: not enough tax revenue compared to its GDP, too much dependence on oil money, and a messy, complicated tax system. To tackle this, the government passed four new bills, including the Nigeria Tax Act (NTA) and set up a new body called the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS). These reforms are designed to make things simpler and fairer. For example, big international companies now have to pay at least 15% in taxes, which brings Nigeria in line with global standards. The tax net has also been widened to include digital assets like crypto, and the personal income tax system is now more progressive meaning people who earn less get more relief. Small businesses get a break too, thanks to a higher exemption threshold. Plus, everything's going digital, with tools like e-invoicing to make tax administration smoother and more transparent. The hope is that these changes will help Nigeria earn more from non-oil sources, reduce its debt, and grow a more diverse economy. But it won't be easy. There's pushback from state governments, tech and infrastructure challenges, and a big need to rebuild public trust through transparency.

AI.tldr: 尼日利亚2025年实施重大税制改革，包括通过《尼日利亚税法》和设立尼日利亚税务局，旨在解决税收收入不足、过度依赖石油收入等问题。改革内容包括对跨国公司征收最低15%税率、扩大数字资产征税范围、实施累进个人所得税制度、提高小微企业免税门槛以及推行电子发票等数字化措施。

title: The SAD Side of Investment Biases
affiliations: Curtin University of Technology - School of Economics and Finance - Department of Finance and Banking, Curtin University - Department of Finance and Banking and Miami University

detail.title: The SAD Side of Investment Biases
detail.abstract: This paper examines how seasonal variation in daylight, via the physiological and psychological effects of Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD), influences retail investor behavior. Using data from over 39,000 U.S. brokerage accounts with detailed trade-level and portfolio holdings, we document that reduced daylight significantly reduces trading activity, performance chasing, and lottery-type stock purchases, while decreasing the disposition effect. These findings are robust across investor types, geographies, alternative proxies for SAD, and placebo tests. Our findings offer micro-level evidence that mood-related physiological shifts systematically modulate behavioral biases, advancing both behavioral finance and the economics of affect.

title: Institutional Resilience and Youth Labor Market Outcomes: Divergent Development Trajectories in Rwanda and the Republic of Congo
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Institutional Resilience and Youth Labor Market Outcomes: Divergent Development Trajectories in Rwanda and the Republic of Congo
detail.abstract: This paper examined how institutional frameworks and resource endowments differentially affect youth employment outcomes in Central Africa. European colonial legacies and natural resource distributions created divergent governance structures that persist in contemporary labor market performance. Rwanda's non-resource-dependent institutions have enabled systematic human capital accumulation and structural transformation, reducing youth unemployment to 18.0% by 2024. Conversely, the Republic of Congo's hydrocarbon dependence produces fiscal volatility that undermines consistent policy implementation, resulting in 41% youth unemployment. Utilizing comparative institutional analysis and labor force data spanning 2017-2024, we demonstrate that governance coherence not resource abundance determines employment generation capacity. Our findings suggest that counter-cyclical fiscal mechanisms and private sector development policies can mitigate resource curse effects on labor absorption.

AI.tldr: 本文研究了制度框架和资源禀赋如何差异性地影响中非青年就业结果。研究发现，治理一致性而非资源丰裕度决定就业创造能力，卢旺达的非资源依赖型制度实现了18%的青年失业率，而刚果共和国的油气依赖导致41%的青年失业率。

AI.motivation: 欧洲殖民遗产和自然资源分布创造了不同的治理结构，这些结构在当代劳动力市场表现中持续存在，需要理解这些差异对青年就业的影响。

title: Revisiting the Distance Elasticity and Investment Motives in the FDI Gravity Model: Aggregate Vs. Sector-Level Evidence
affiliations: University of Groningen - Faculty of Economics and Business

detail.title: Revisiting the Distance Elasticity and Investment Motives in the FDI Gravity Model: Aggregate Vs. Sector-Level Evidence
detail.abstract: This paper re-examines foreign direct investment motives in the ‘FDI gravity’ model (Kleinert and Toubal, 2010), focusing on the role of distance. More precisely, we investigate whether aggregate and pooled gravity models for FDI obscure relevant heterogeneities across sectors. This is possible through the novel MREID dataset, which provides us with FDI data at the 2-digit NAICS level for 184 countries over the period 2010 to 2020. Our results reveal that aggregate and pooled models mask significant sector heterogeneities in two aspects: (i) in the importance of horizontal versus vertical FDI motives, and (ii) in the distance elasticity. The latter reflects that distance potentially captures more complex sector-specific components than are captured in the current gravity model for FDI.

AI.tldr: 本文重新检验了FDI引力模型中外国直接投资动机，重点关注距离的作用。研究发现，总体和汇总的引力模型掩盖了跨行业的重要异质性，特别是在水平与垂直FDI动机的重要性以及距离弹性方面。
AI.research_question: 总体和汇总的FDI引力模型是否掩盖了跨行业的相关异质性？
AI.motivation: 重新审视FDI引力模型中的投资动机，特别关注距离的作用，并探讨现有模型是否忽略了行业层面的重要差异。
AI.theoretical_framework: FDI引力模型（Kleinert和Toubal，2010），水平与垂直FDI动机理论
AI.method: 使用新颖的MREID数据集，包含2010-2020年184个国家2位数NAICS级别的FDI数据，进行行业层面的异质性分析
AI.findings: 总体和汇总模型掩盖了显著的行业异质性：1）水平与垂直FDI动机重要性的差异；2）距离弹性的差异。距离可能捕捉了比当前FDI引力模型更复杂的行业特定组成部分。
AI.theory_contributions: 揭示了FDI引力模型中行业异质性的重要性，挑战了总体模型的适用性，为理解距离在FDI中的复杂作用提供了新视角。
AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者和投资者提供了更细致的行业层面FDI模式分析，有助于更精准的投资决策和政策设计。

title: Estimating Interaction Effects with Panel Data
affiliations: McMaster University and University of Groningen - Faculty of Economics and Business

detail.title: Estimating Interaction Effects with Panel Data
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes how interaction effects can be consistently estimated under economically plausible assumptions in linear panel models with a fixed Tdimension. We advocate for a correlated interaction term estimator (CITE) and show that it is consistent under conditions that are not sufficient for consistency of the interaction term estimator that is most common in applied econometric work. Our paper discusses the empirical content of these conditions, shows that standard inference procedures can be applied to CITE, and analyzes consistency, relative efficiency, inference, and their finite sample properties in a simulation study. In an empirical application, we test whether labor displacement effects of robots are stronger in countries at higher income levels. The results are in line with our theoretical and simulation results and indicate that standard interaction term estimation underestimates the importance of a country's income level in the relationship between robots and employment and may prematurely reject a null hypothesis about interaction effects in the presence of misspecification.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种相关交互项估计器（CITE），在线性面板模型中能够一致地估计交互效应，比应用计量经济学中最常见的交互项估计器具有更宽松的一致性条件。

AI.theoretical_framework: 线性面板模型，固定时间维度，相关交互项估计器（CITE）的理论框架

title: Bridging Minds and Markets: A Historical and Analytical Study of Economic Psychology and Behavioral Economics (work in progress)
affiliations: Comillas Pontifical University - Faculty of Economics and Business Administration

detail.title: Bridging Minds and Markets: A Historical and Analytical Study of Economic Psychology and Behavioral Economics (work in progress)
detail.abstract: Behavioral economics, thanks to contributions from the science of Psychology, has progressively transformed economics itself, moving it from a theory based on extreme rationality proposed by classical and neoclassical economists to a science of human behavior. This article traces its intellectual evolution, beginning with the moral philosophy of Adam Smith and David Hume, continuing with the "old" behavioral programs of Herbert Simon and George Katona, and culminating in the "new" behavioral revolution led mainly by Daniel Kahneman, Amos Tversky, Richard Thaler, Vernon Smith, and Robert Shiller. Drawing on both historical and analytical perspectives, it attempts to build a dialogue between psychology and economics, to understand the methodological variations that shaped this field and how we see its expansion today, from individual and social knowledge to finance and public policy. This article concludes that this recent branch of economics now provides a more realistic microeconomic foundation for understanding choices, institutions, and collective welfare.

AI.tldr: 本文追溯了行为经济学的思想演变历程，从亚当·斯密和大卫·休谟的道德哲学开始，经过赫伯特·西蒙和乔治·卡托纳的"旧"行为经济学项目，到丹尼尔·卡尼曼、阿莫斯·特沃斯基、理查德·塞勒、弗农·史密斯和罗伯特·希勒领导的"新"行为革命。文章通过历史和理论分析，构建了心理学与经济学的对话，探讨了该领域的方法论变迁及其在个体与社会认知、金融和公共政策等领域的扩展。
AI.research_question: 行为经济学如何从心理学中汲取养分，逐步改变经济学本身，从古典和新古典经济学提出的极端理性理论转向对人类行为的科学研究？
AI.motivation: 传统经济学基于极端理性假设，而行为经济学通过引入心理学视角，为经济学提供了更现实的微观基础，以更好地理解选择、制度和集体福利。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于亚当·斯密和大卫·休谟的道德哲学、赫伯特·西蒙和乔治·卡托纳的"旧"行为经济学理论，以及丹尼尔·卡尼曼、阿莫斯·特沃斯基等人的"新"行为经济学理论框架。
AI.method: 采用历史和理论分析相结合的方法，构建心理学与经济学的对话，探讨方法论变迁和领域扩展。
AI.findings: 行为经济学已经发展成为一个更现实的微观经济学基础，能够更好地解释个体选择、制度设计和集体福利问题，其应用已扩展到金融和公共政策等领域。
AI.theory_contributions: 为经济学提供了更现实的微观基础，挑战了传统经济学的极端理性假设，促进了心理学与经济学的跨学科融合。
AI.practical_contributions: 行为经济学的见解已被广泛应用于金融决策、公共政策设计和制度优化等领域，为实际问题的解决提供了新的视角和方法。

detail.title: Road-Mapping Generative AI (GenAI) and Its Impact: AI for Whom and for What?
detail.abstract: This introductory chapter outlines the conceptual foundations, objectives, and structure of Multidisciplinary Movements in AI and Generative AI, situating the rapid evolution of AI and GenAI within broader societal, political, and economic transformations. It highlights how current debates—spanning governance, ethics, education, and business—are shaped by decentralization, Web3 technologies, and the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The chapter addresses the persistent gap between technical discourse and the real-world implications of AI, emphasizing the need for interdisciplinary, accessible analyses that support informed decision-making across sectors. Through case studies bridging the Global North and Global South, the book examines AI’s potential to empower communities while also exposing risks related to inequality, opacity, and democratic erosion. It advances a roadmap for responsible and inclusive AI, underscoring trust-building, accountability, and human-centric governance as prerequisites for resilient and sustainable futures. By framing the question “AI for whom and for what?”, the chapter positions the volume as a resource for scholars, policymakers, educators, and practitioners seeking to navigate the societal impact of AI and GenAI and ensure that their benefits are equitably distributed.

title: The Informational Role of Corporate Disclosure in Commodity Markets

detail.title: The Informational Role of Corporate Disclosure in Commodity Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no conflicts of interest to declare.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the informativeness of corporate disclosure from the commodity market's perspective. I find that both realized revenues and management revenue forecasts, when aggregated across firms exposed to commodity price risks, are strong positive predictors of future commodity returns. Their predictive power is stronger when revenue signals are more precise and weaker in markets where information on commodity fundamentals is more transparent. Further, I show that their information content is useful: even simple long-short trading strategies generate significantly positive returns. I also show that revenue disclosures influence the short-term price discovery process, indicating that they provide timely signals. Overall, my findings suggest that revenue disclosures convey incremental information about commodity fundamentals, yet commodity markets underreact to this information.

title: When the Tide Goes Out: The Effect of QE on the Structure of the Financial System
affiliations: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority, Boston College,  and Harvard Business School

detail.title: When the Tide Goes Out: The Effect of QE on the Structure of the Financial System
detail.abstract: This paper shows that the prolonged period of low long-term interest rates fundamentally reshaped the European financial system by compressing the life-insurance sector-the main private holder of long-dated sovereign debt. Life insurers depend on high longterm yields to offer attractive guaranteed-return savings products to households. Using newly assembled supervisory data from EIOPA combined with flow-of-funds statistics, we show that the compression of term premia under quantitative easing (QE) reduced household inflows into life insurers by nearly EUR 2 trillion between 2015 and 2022, leading to a sharp contraction in their bond holdings. Instrumenting the term premium with high-frequency monetary policy shocks, we find that insurers' inflows respond strongly to long-term rates, particularly among those most exposed to guaranteed-rate products. Because insurers invest roughly EUR 0.70 in bonds for every EUR 1 of inflows, this liability-side channel accounts for the bulk of their bond demand. The effects during QT were not symmetric: rising rates triggered widespread policy surrenders, turning insurers into net sellers of government bonds. Although inflows have begun to recover as yields normalized, the rebound remains limited. By compressing long-term yields, QE indirectly reshaped the investor base for sovereign debt-leaving bond markets more reliant on central bank demand and less anchored by private long-term investors.

detail.title: Why Housing and Groceries Remain so Expensive in 2025
detail.abstract: In 2025, Americans are facing abhorrently high costs for two of life's most basic necessities, housing and groceries. According to Economic Research Service of the United States Department of Agriculture, retail food-price inflation is expected to continue. The nonprofit Prosperity Now reports that in January 2025 alone, grocery store prices rose 0.5 percent and housing costs accounted for a little over 30 percent of the overall monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index. Why are housing and groceries so expensive right now? Regarding groceries, multiple factors take place including disease outbreaks, global trade shocks, greed, and weather events. The housing market has similar factors but was impacted differently. This paper will look at the different contributing factors to the high cost of living in America today.

title: Emerging Markets: The Case of Brazil
affiliations: , Columbia University in the City of New York, Columbia University in the City of New York, Columbia University in the City of New York and Columbia University in the City of New York

detail.title: Emerging Markets: The Case of Brazil
detail.abstract: Brazil, Latin America's largest economy, has been experiencing slow economic recovery from its 2015-16 recession amid the Covid-19 pandemic. Strong policy response and critical reforms by the government have helped to cushion the effects of the pandemic, and the overall macroeconomic and financial indicators remain solid in an environment of low interest rates and inflation. External indicators are considered resilient, including continued direct investment inflows, which would act as a buffer to potential volatility. Brazil's financial sector has recovered from the recession due to positive growth in private credit. The government has improved credit conditions leading to increased credit issued by large, corporate companies and growing household credit. Despite the growing concern on Brazil's peaking public debt position, we believe that Brazil's reform agendas are expected to shore up public finances and help to maintain debt sustainability in the future.

title: Ctrl + Alt + Justice, Rebooting the Justice Delivery System: A Case for 24 *7 Online Courts, Its Feasibility and Legality

detail.title: Ctrl + Alt + Justice, Rebooting the Justice Delivery System: A Case for 24 *7 Online Courts, Its Feasibility and Legality

declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as part of the Feasibility report prepared for the Hon'ble Madras High Court in behalf of Centre for Justice through Technology at VMLS, Chennai.

detail.abstract:
India’s courts are carrying a staggering backlog of cases, which has made delays an unavoidable part of ordinary life for litigants. This paper asks a simple but urgent question: can online courts that operate twenty four hours a day genuinely change this reality. The study takes the Kollam 24×7 ON Court pilot as its starting point and uses it to explore what an always available digital courtroom could mean for access to justice in India. Drawing on comparative experiences from China, the United Kingdom, Canada, Singapore, and other jurisdictions, the paper shows how online courts elsewhere have made legal processes quicker, more accessible, and less burdensome for users who often have work, family, and distance constraints.

The analysis then turns to Indian law and demonstrates that the shift to online courts fits comfortably within existing statutory and judicial frameworks, including the Information Technology Act, the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, the CPC and BNSS provisions on virtual participation, and Supreme Court guidelines that have already recognized electronic evidence and video hearings as legally valid.

The paper keeps the human impact at the center of the discussion. It considers what it means for a litigant to avoid repeated travel to the courthouse, for a lawyer to conduct routine hearings without losing hours in crowded corridors, and for judges to manage their dockets with better tools. It also takes seriously the concerns about digital access and infrastructure and proposes a phased set of reforms, beginning with focused pilots and supported by training, hybrid options, and clear procedural safeguards.

The study concludes that twenty four by seven online courts are not a distant or speculative idea. India already possesses the legal and administrative foundation to support them, and the early evidence from Kollam shows their practical promise. If implemented with care and attention to users, they can help create a justice system that is quicker, more transparent, and easier for people to navigate.

AI.tldr: 该论文探讨24小时在线法庭能否解决印度法院案件积压问题，通过Kollam试点项目分析数字法庭对司法可及性的影响，并基于比较法研究提出分阶段改革建议。

AI.method: 案例研究法（以Kollam 24×7 ON Court试点为研究对象），比较法分析，法律文本分析。

title: Monetary Policy-Embedded Currency Options: A Generalized Garman-Kohlhagen Model under Taylor Rules
affiliations: Comillas Pontifical University - Faculty of Economics and Business Administration

detail.title: Monetary Policy-Embedded Currency Options: A Generalized Garman-Kohlhagen Model under Taylor Rules
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a generalized extension of the Garman-Kohlhagen (1983) currency option pricing model by endogenizing the domestic risk-free rate through a Taylor rule function. Unlike traditional models that assume constant interest rates, our "GK-Taylor" framework explicitly incorporates monetary policy reactions to inflation and output gaps into the option's pricing kernel. This modification allows Central Banks-particularly those in inflation-targeting regimes-to utilize currency options not merely as hedging instruments, but as strategic policy tools to anchor market expectations and stabilize exchange rates. We derive and verify the specific "Greeks" associated with macro-monetary variables, providing policymakers with precise sensitivity measures. Numerical simulations confirm that standard models significantly misprice options during periods of inflationary stress, whereas the GK-Taylor model captures the implied cost of monetary reaction.

title: From Courtrooms to Shop Floors: How Judicial Independence Shapes Employee Treatment
affiliations: Shanghai University, Shanghai University, Shanghai University and Tsinghua University - School of Social Sciences

detail.title: From Courtrooms to Shop Floors: How Judicial Independence Shapes Employee Treatment
detail.abstract: This paper examines how judicial independence shapes firms’ treatment of employees by exploiting China’s circuit court reform as a quasi-natural experiment. Using a difference-in-differences design, we find that enhanced judicial independence leads to significant improvements in employee treatment. Mechanism analyses reveal that firms improve employee treatment in response to heightened litigation risk following judicial reforms. Heterogeneity analyses show that the effect is stronger in firms previously shielded from legal accountability, such as state-owned enterprises, politically connected firms, and those operating in regions with stronger local protectionism, suggesting that judicial independence recalibrates corporate incentives where legal enforcement was historically weak. Additionally, the effect is amplified in firms with stronger union presence and greater public scrutiny, highlighting complementary institutional forces. This study highlights judicial independence as a critical determinant of employee welfare, offering valuable insights for developing economies seeking to improve labor standards through institutional reforms beyond mere legislative changes.

title: Imputation-Powered Inference for Missing Covariates

detail.title: Imputation-Powered Inference for Missing Covariates
detail.abstract: Missing covariate data is a prevalent problem in empirical research. We provide a novel framework for handling missing covariate data for estimation and inference in downstream tasks. Our general framework provides an automatic and easy-to-use pipeline for empirical researchers: First, missing values are imputed using virtually any imputation method under general observation patterns. Second, we automatically correct for the imputation bias and adaptively weight the imputed values according to their quality. Third, we use all available data, including imputed observations, to obtain more precise point estimates for the downstream task with valid confidence intervals. Our approach ensures valid inference while improving statistical efficiency by leveraging all available data. We establish the asymptotic normality of the proposed estimator under general missing data patterns and a broad class of imputation methods. Through simulations, we demonstrate the superior performance of our approach over natural benchmarks, as it achieves both lower bias and variance while being robust to imputation quality. In a comprehensive empirical study of the dependence of equity markets on carbon emissions, we show that properly accounting for missing emissions data yields no evidence of correlation between stock returns and emissions directly produced by companies, but a negative correlation with value chain emissions.

detail.abstract: The Middle Eastern studies within African universities, both public and private, have increasing academic, policy and research significance. Africa and the Middle East share centuries of intertwined and interconnected history — from trans-Saharan trade and Islamic scholarship to modern political and economic cooperation. Nevertheless, African higher education has often treated “Middle Eastern Studies” (MES) as peripheral, despite its clear relevance to the continent’s historical, cultural, and geopolitical realities. This article argues and contends that MES is academically relevant for African universities because it deepens historical understanding, enhances linguistic and religious literacy, informs development and diplomacy, and fosters interdisciplinary research that links Africa to the wider world.

detail.title: Banking Without Banks in Canada: Banking-as-a-Service Disruption and Regulatory Gaps
detail.abstract: In recent years, scholars and leading policymaking institutions (e.g., Bank of England; Bank for International Settlement) have shifted their understanding of banking and money away from a simple financial intermediation model towards a recognition that in modern market economies, the banking sector is the major "place" where new monetary units are created. This study examines the significant regulatory challenges posed by Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) within Canada's financial technology ecosystem. BaaS fundamentally reconfigures the banking value chain by decoupling customer-facing services and product delivery from the licensed financial institutions that hold the balance sheets and regulatory licenses. This disaggregation allows non-bank entities, often fintechs, to facilitate a range of financial activities, including those indirectly linked to credit creation and payment processing, frequently operating with less comprehensive oversight than traditional deposit-taking and lending institutions. The paper argues that this structural shift exacerbates existing regulatory ambiguities in Canada, particularly those stemming from the constitutional division of powers between federal and provincial authorities over banking and commerce. Employing a qualitative and analytical research design, the study synthesizes insights from relevant theoretical frameworks on money and banking, a detailed analysis of Canadian legal and regulatory documents, and a comparative examination of regulatory approaches adopted in the European Union, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Furthermore, the research incorporates empirical evidence from an analysis of Canadian users' online reviews of prominent fintech platforms, which reveals notable consumer confusion regarding the nature and extent of deposit protection and the identity of the regulated entity. Findings highlight critical gaps in accountability frameworks and challenges in ensuring consistent consumer protection and systemic stability across complex BaaS value chains. Key policy actions proposed include mandating enhanced transparency and standardized consumer protection disclosures, particularly concerning deposit insurance clarity; establishing clear joint liability mechanisms for fintech-bank partnerships to ensure accountability; and progressively moving towards a more functional, activitybased regulatory framework.

detail.abstract: This research unveils a critical thermodynamic law governing development finance: financial energy is subject to irreversible entropy generation, systematically dissipating within governance systems before conversion into public goods. Challenging conventional aid models, we demonstrate that the core problem is not merely the volume of funding but the efficiency of its conversion, a dimension largely ignored in prior literature. Our groundbreaking empirical analysis, using an original global panel dataset, yields three transformative observations. First, we establish a new metric for "irreversible loss," revealing an average 35% efficiency gap in WASH sectors. Second, we provide causal evidence that democratic accountability is not a mere correlate but a powerful moderator, with a significant positive interaction effect (β = 0.029, p < 0.05) showing that finance only achieves its potential in accountable systems. Third, we document this phenomenon in both composite efficiency and physical infrastructure, demonstrating that democracy reduces physical water loss (β = -1.842, p < 0.05). These findings fundamentally redefine aid effectiveness, shifting the paradigm from conditional input-outcome models to a thermodynamic theory of political conversion efficiency. The policy implication is revolutionary: without concomitant investment in democratic accountability, a significant portion of global development finance is thermodynamically destined for dissipation, irrevocably lost to its human development goals.

detail.title: Liquidity-Robust Linear Programming for Turnover-Constrained Portfolio Rebalancing
detail.abstract: This paper develops a linear programming framework for single-period portfolio rebalancing under explicit turnover and liquidity constraints. The central object is a liquidity-adjusted turnover polytope which captures joint restrictions on transaction size, factor exposure, and gross trading volume. Within this polyhedral environment, we introduce a class of linear programs whose dual variables admit a clear financial interpretation as shadow prices of turnover and liquidity. The main contribution is a family of representation results: (i) the marginal value of an additional unit of turnover budget coincides with the dual price of a single linear constraint; (ii) liquidity tightening corresponds to a collection of binding box-constraints whose dual variables aggregate into an adversarial liquidity cost index. We derive monotonicity and convexity properties of the optimal value with respect to turnover and liquidity parameters, and we characterize when turnover constraints are non-binding. Finally, we outline an empirical implementation in an equity universe and provide templates for numerical experiments.

detail.title: The Economics of Climate Talk in Real Estate: Real Effects and Financial Performance
detail.abstract: We investigate the economic consequences of corporate climate change dialogue using text-based exposure measures from earnings conference calls for U.S. public real estate firms. We find that this dialogue is a powerful leading indicator of tangible corporate transition actions. Higher regulatory exposure predicts future investment in certified green buildings and attracts tenants with superior environmental profiles. This transition, however, entails short-term costs. Higher opportunity exposure, in contrast, predicts a persistent decline in future operating and rental performance. While these cash flow risks are priced, leading to a subsequent significant valuation discount, higher opportunity exposure is associated with lower future realized stock returns, suggesting market underreaction to the severity of predictable cash flow decline. Our findings highlight the critical need for adaptive strategies that balance environmental goals with financial performance, especially as regulatory pressures and market expectations about sustainability continue to evolve.

title: Neuro Risk Impact Assessment (NRIA): Integrating Neurotech Ethics into Military Strategic Planning Frameworks
affiliations: KDI School of Public Policy and Management

detail.title: Neuro Risk Impact Assessment (NRIA): Integrating Neurotech Ethics into Military Strategic Planning Frameworks
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of neurotechnology in defense research, human-machine teaming, and operational planning has created ethical, legal, and humanitarian risks that current governance frameworks cannot address. These technologies interact directly with neural activity and mental states, raising concerns about autonomy, mental privacy, dual-use misuse, and compliance with international humanitarian law. This paper introduces the Neuro Risk Impact Assessment (NRIA), a novel structured pre-deployment governance model adapted from Environmental and Social Impact Assessment methodologies. NRIA operationalizes principles from UNESCO, the OECD, the ICRC, and UNIDIR into six assessment dimensions: autonomy and well-being, mental-privacy protection, safety and dual-use risk, legal compliance, operational reliability, and impacts on peace and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Open-source reporting on programmes such as the U.S. DARPA Next-Generation Nonsurgical Neurotechnology (N3) initiative and China's brain-machine interface research, along with the fact that only 39 countries have adhered to the OECD Neurotechnology Recommendation since 2019 (OECD, 2025), signals the need for such a framework. NRIA does not endorse any form of military neurotechnology or its integration with Artificial Intelligence (AI); it aims to prevent harmful, or rights eroding uses through structured oversight.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种新型的神经风险影响评估框架，用于解决神经技术在军事应用中引发的伦理、法律和人道主义风险。
AI.research_question: 如何开发一个结构化的治理框架来评估和减轻军事神经技术部署中的伦理、法律和人道主义风险？
AI.motivation: 神经技术在国防研究、人机协同和作战规划中的快速扩张，带来了现有治理框架无法解决的伦理、法律和人道主义风险。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于环境和社会影响评估方法，整合联合国教科文组织、经合组织、红十字国际委员会和联合国裁军研究所的原则。
AI.method: 开发神经风险影响评估模型，包含六个评估维度：自主权与福祉、心理隐私保护、安全与双重用途风险、法律合规性、操作可靠性、对和平与可持续发展目标的影响。
AI.findings: 现有治理框架不足，仅有39个国家采纳了经合组织的神经技术建议，迫切需要结构化的风险评估框架。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了首个专门针对军事神经技术的结构化治理模型，将国际原则操作化为具体评估维度。
AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者和军事机构提供了实用的风险评估工具，防止有害或侵犯人权的神经技术应用。

title: Hybrid Multimodal Learning Framework for Crop Disease Detection, Adaptive Treatment, and Price Forecasting
affiliations: Vishwakarma Institute of Information Technology (VIIT), Amity University, Dubai, UAE, Symbiosis Institute of Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Hybrid Multimodal Learning Framework for Crop Disease Detection, Adaptive Treatment, and Price Forecasting
detail.abstract: Crop diseases threaten global food security and require fast, accurate, and scalable diagnostic solutions that surpass slow and inconsistent human inspection. This study presents a Hybrid Multimodal Learning framework that unifies image-based disease diagnosis, treatment recommendation, and market price forecasting in a single, deployable system. The diagnostic model employs a dual-stream architecture combining EfficientNetB0 image embeddings with environmental/tabular inputs, achieving 99.95% accuracy, 99.92% precision, 99.96% F1-score, and 99.93% recall on the tomato disease dataset. Comparative evaluation across YOLOv8, ResNet50, EfficientNetB0, and a custom CNN confirms EfficientNetB0 as the most robust and generalizable model. Edge-AI experiments demonstrate that INT8 quantization on Jetson devices significantly improves inference speed with negligible accuracy loss, supporting real-time field deployment. A knowledge-driven pesticide recommendation engine suggests sustainable treatments based on symptoms and environmental factors. Additionally, an LSTM forecasting module achieves 3.2%–4.1% MAE, offering actionable market insights. SHAP and LIME provide transparency, improving user trust. Overall, this modular system enables efficient, data-driven crop management. Key methods used are:               •             Dual-stream multimodal architecture               •             INT8 Edge-AI optimization               •             LSTM market forecasting

AI.tldr: 本研究提出了一个混合多模态学习框架，统一了基于图像的作物病害诊断、治疗建议和市场预测，在番茄病害数据集上达到99.95%准确率，支持边缘AI实时部署。
AI.research_question: 如何开发一个统一、可部署的系统来快速准确诊断作物病害并提供治疗建议和市场预测？
AI.motivation: 作物病害威胁全球粮食安全，需要超越缓慢且不一致的人工检查的快速、准确、可扩展的诊断解决方案。
AI.theoretical_framework: 混合多模态学习框架，结合计算机视觉、环境因素分析和时间序列预测理论。
AI.method: 双流多模态架构（EfficientNetB0图像嵌入+环境/表格输入）、INT8边缘AI优化、LSTM市场预测、SHAP和LIME可解释性分析。
AI.findings: 诊断模型在番茄病害数据集上达到99.95%准确率；INT8量化显著提升推理速度且精度损失可忽略；LSTM预测模块MAE为3.2%-4.1%。

AI.practical_contributions: 开发了可部署的实时作物管理系统，包含知识驱动的农药推荐引擎和可操作的市场洞察，提高了用户信任度。

title: The Lifetime Price of Harm: Economic Costs of Sexual Violence and the Case for Timely Intervention in Australia
affiliations: University of Western Australia and The University of Western Australia - UWA Business School

detail.title: The Lifetime Price of Harm: Economic Costs of Sexual Violence and the Case for Timely Intervention in Australia

declarations.funderStatement: This project was funded by Allambee

detail.abstract:
In 2021-22, there were an estimated 150,000 cases of sexual abuse towards children aged 0-17 and a further 114,000 cases of sexual assault to women aged 18 and over in Australia costing a total of $7.5 billion and $6.6 billion over the life course.

Sexual violence is a pervasive issue in Australia, having not only acute immediate impacts on victim-survivors and their families but across different services and systems. Australian governments at the commonwealth and state-levels have made considerable reform and funding commitments to the broader issues of family and domestic violence against women and children, with a proportion of this effort being directed at sexual violence.

As part of the growing calls for effective intervention is a renewed emphasis on the part of advocates and governments to better understand the comprehensive costs of sexual violence on individuals, society and the economy. The analysis undertaken in this report aims to estimate the short and long-term costs attributable to sexual violence within the Australian population. Through the estimation of childhood sexual abuse (CSA, years 0-17) and adult sexual assault (ASA, years 18+) prevalence, the annual and lifetime, that is the costs borne over a person’s life rather than immediately, costs are presented and the implications discussed. By estimating both the annual and lifetime expenditure across the economy, the report contributes to the economic case for proactive and sustained intervention into addressing sexual violence across Australia.
